contract_distinction.finding: The inherited 57-register contract measures the complete CPU of the original-instruction execution engine. It is not, by itself, a demand to capture every privileged register of the host running the original game. The subsequent raw64 compatibility envelope is necessary for the chosen route importing/restoring an actual WOW64 machine context, not automatically for every valid implementation route.

Equally, do not require native CR/hidden-cache acquisition merely to execute the already declared guest engine against correctly owned real platform leaves. These are different source contracts.

child_VEH_limits.state: XSTATE beyond the fixed base CONTEXT
child_VEH_limits.reason: The fixture copies CONTEXT by value into fixed records (716 bytes), despite an exception flag indicating XSTATE. Windows provides size/alignment-aware allocation, CopyContext, feature masks and LocateXStateFeature. Validity and INIT semantics must be recorded. A later context read of a thread already executing VEH is not automatically the saved fault context.

child_VEH_limits.classification: not supplied by this user-mode context API; direct privileged-register access cannot be added as ordinary CPL3 instructions
child_VEH_limits.reason: WOW64_CONTEXT has no CR fields. DR4/5 are not independent universally readable values; semantics depend on CR4.DE. A separate authorized privileged/virtualization source would be needed for a complete actual-machine claim. This finding does not apply to existing guest-engine registers, whose source is the engine itself.

child_VEH_limits.state: Descriptor tables, selectors and hidden segment caches
child_VEH_limits.classification: must distinguish readable descriptor-table entries from cached hardware state
child_VEH_limits.reason: Wow64GetThreadSelectorEntry can retrieve a table entry, so claiming all segment information is inherently unreadable is false. It does not certify the loaded hidden cache. Intel documents that cached descriptors can differ from memory-resident descriptors. Some descriptor-table store instructions are conditionally available in user mode; they still cannot supply this entire original fault-time envelope or guarantee same CPU/instant.
child_VEH_limits.local: devtools/terminal_scene_owner.py:159-170 uses the selector-entry API in capture_tls for bounded TEB provenance; docs/terminal_wait_child_veh.md:60-63

child_VEH_limits.state: Upper GPR halves, R8-R15, XMM8-XMM15 and original compatibility-mode envelope
child_VEH_limits.classification: unimplemented and unqualified in the x86 VEH route; not proven universally impossible
child_VEH_limits.reason: WOW64_CONTEXT omits these fields. Native x64 CONTEXT exposes additional register fields, but simply requesting that context while the target is executing VEH/WOW64 exception machinery does not authenticate the original stopped compatibility-mode instant. No bridge in this review proves the required correspondence.

child_VEH_limits.classification: unqualified even if missing context fields are added
child_VEH_limits.reason: A successful first-consumer stop and one consumption prove a synchronous boundary, not full pre-exception equivalence or continuous original instruction/write/ABI history. VEH executes code, writes a stack/records and changes scheduling. The fixture restores debug registers and preserves supplied base-context bytes, not an independently known full pre-exception state.

deployment_review.existing_mechanism: tools/school_scheduler_lifetime.py:34-84 contains an owned-process private-buffer bridge: VirtualAllocEx, writes restricted to fresh allocations, RW-to-RX protection/cache flush, CreateRemoteThread, bounded entry/ABI checks, wait/exit verification and no freeing active code. docs/school_scheduler_lifetime.md:13-17 and 30-51 record historical isolated-object native success with original code/IAT preserved.
deployment_review.not_a_ready_VEH_installer: The bridge whitelist does not include AddVectoredExceptionHandler. Its historical technical scope was isolated private scheduler objects; it does not establish current game exception-chain equivalence or safe registration/removal. The fixture registers its handler only in its own purpose-built Child (devtools/terminal_wait_child_veh_fixture.cpp:145), not in the game. No dormant original startup stub or preinstalled original-game VEH was identified in the reviewed implementation. Existing session authorization is a separate question and is not assumed absent here.
deployment_review.risk: Even writing only new private buffers is a process mutation. Registration changes exception handling; a new thread changes timing/layout and invokes DLL notifications. Installing with First=1 changes handler ordering. Removal and quiescence must precede code deallocation. Startup CREATE_SUSPENDED is not automatically safe: remote threads may not begin until DLL initialization finishes.
deployment_review.decision: Do not claim deployment impossible merely because no current installer exists. The decisive blockers are technical qualification of the current parent/handler chain, safe teardown, and the insufficient actual-machine state/trajectory source. Current full-state no-go makes deploying this candidate a poor next step for complete acceptance, regardless of permission.

preferred_route_review.route: Return to the existing original-instruction engine and close its current-owner/platform boundary, preserving its full CPU/ABI/memory/trace checks. Native game observation remains corroborating evidence unless a complete native import is independently qualified.
actual_first_dependencies: docs/terminal_wait.md:7-14: the retained TASK first 0x30 bytes and MAIN scheduler region are zero; 4223A8 would pass 0x100 to EnterCriticalSection. An observer cannot turn that into a valid owner.

docs/terminal_wait.md:24: the retained 4539B0 root returns to a sentinel and lacks actual 451AB7/451711/421F88 ancestors. The next fresh source must generate those ancestors naturally; restoring the old tail cannot manufacture them.

devtools/terminal_wait_registration_probe.py:78-84,210-225,288-300: original construction reaches 56E0BE with [0,0,56E110,current PTD,4,node+24] and exact 116-byte PTD, but heap/PTD and scheduler events are in two helper processes. No CreateThread executes.

tools/school_retained_scheduler_platform.cs:26-34 serves leaves on one serial command thread, has no worker support and bounds wait to 1000 ms. It cannot supply concurrent original MAIN/worker semantics by merely removing a guard or returning success.

tools/school_crt_init_platform.cs:40-56 likewise serves heap/critical leaves on its single command thread. Real lock ownership, TLS, thread identity and blocked waits need per-source-thread routing in one current owner.
preferred_route_review.why_not_disproved: The inherited proof already permits explicit real OS-leaf ABI translation while retaining guest architecture. Windows CreateThread requires code/parameter in its owning process; it does not require copying privileged host registers into an emulator. The project already proved original CRT/scheduler native lifetimes for private objects. The missing integration is concrete ownership/execution routing, not a known Windows prohibition.
preferred_route_review.why_not_already_go: Unifying the two helper binaries alone is insufficient. The start address 56E110 is a guest code address, PTD/node/MAIN pointers have guest ownership, and thread-local operations/critical sections must execute on the corresponding real worker. A generic event-only helper or a fabricated callback return violates the contract. No reviewed implementation currently supplies the complete bridge and independent trace.
bounded_next_step: Read/derive the exact original 56E110 -> TLS installation -> 421F50 -> virtual callback chain, with native leaf operations and logical/native pointer roles; select one fresh owned address space and explicit per-thread routing before changing code.

Implement only the smallest same-owner creation/resume/first-yield path after that mapping is reviewable: a real suspended OS thread must cause original wrapper and callback instructions to execute, with their full guest CPU and writes recorded. If execution is interpreter-driven, its trampoline must dispatch original instructions, never replace the callback with a waiting stub. This is a candidate platform architecture and needs explicit independent acceptance, not a claimed existing feature.

The gate ends after the original manager/node handshake returns successfully, with real PID/TID/TLS/PTD/lock ownership and normal cleanup. Reject wrong owner, failed wait, missing original wrapper/callback execution, or unexplained memory/state projection. Do not run the long battle prefix before this gate passes.

Then create a fresh source from original 451170/451080 construction and real ancestors; reconstruct the two retained logical cases through their current native resource lifetimes. Continue naturally through 422360 and 453CB5/4967B0 without a new consumer root. Preserve both independent complete replays, cumulative hashes, all state and cleanup requirements.

proposed_first_gate_budget.scope: one fresh owner, one real suspended worker, original wrapper/TLS/callback execution through the first original cooperative yield and its matching scheduler signal; no battle prefix or UI
proposed_first_gate_budget.budget_behavior: The outer deadline does not replace INFINITE in the original WaitForSingleObject ABI. A deadline or forced cleanup is a rejected feasibility attempt, never normal original cleanup or a reason to extend/repeat the same recipe.
proposed_first_gate_budget.first_stop_loss: Before ResumeThread require the fresh owner, real worker handle/TID, original 56E110 execution entry, exact current PTD allocation/parameter and thread-specific leaf routing; otherwise reject. TLS is not required to exist before its original installation: after resumption, the original wrapper must execute its actual TlsSetValue and subsequent current-thread lookup on that worker, with its lock ownership and live-object identity verified. Reject at the first missing original instruction/leaf/ownership witness; do not move the gate to a later successful event.

preferred_route_review.same_owner_bridge_status: conditional-go for bounded design/implementation investigation; compatibility with strict original-thread semantics and full retained-resource integration remains unknown until actual evidence exists
